scope: Five prompts, one conversation, Pro bundle key, hosted https://mcp.zovo.one/mcp/catalogue only, on an empty tenant with the shared business profile set first (Voss Electrical, EUR, VAT 23). A small trades business: a three-row price ladder whose newest row is booked for a date still in the future, a labour rate, one deliberately UNDATED 'what do we charge today' question (the round 37 miss, asked twice: as the tail of prompt one and again alone as prompt two), one dated question with a pre-ladder date, one lines_resolve producing both payloads on a real VAT rate, and a price list download. 18 checks, one point each. Token: a Pro bundle key signed locally with node scripts/sign-license.mjs '*' (tenant lic:ba28f06b907c, whoami tier pro, /verify ok), because the round needs price_list_pdf, which is Pro; the tenant was empty at the start (sku_list count 0) and the shared profile was set before any prompt by business_set on /mcp/invoice with the same bearer: Voss Electrical, 8 Mill Lane, Gdansk, EUR, default_tax_rate 23, Europe/Warsaw. Allowlist: 12 explicit mcp__catalogue__<tool> entries read from a live tools/list of that endpoint on that token (sku_set, sku_get, sku_list, sku_delete, rate_set, rate_get, lines_resolve, price_list_text, price_list_pdf, catalogue_report, license_status, license_activate), no mcp__* wildcard. Fresh XDG_DATA_HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME and XDG_STATE_HOME under /private/tmp/uv-r38cat/xdg for every claude invocation (there is no server env block on an http entry, so the XDG pins apply to the client only). npm_config_cache=/Users/mike/.npm-cache-local and PATH prefixed with $HOME/.npm-global/bin. Each prompt its own invocation under timeout 240 with </dev/null on stdin, stdout written to disk per prompt (out/p<n>.json) and read back before the next prompt ran. All five returned rc 0, is_error false and permission_denials empty; durations 23.2 s, 3.0 s, 9.3 s, 26.3 s, 20.3 s. 13 tool calls reached the server across the five prompts (plus 4 client-side ToolSearch calls that never leave the CLI). rubric: 18 named checks across five prompts, one point each, 18 max. A check passes only when the client text and the wire agree: the model's figure is quoted, the tool result or the after-round curl re-derivation on the same token is quoted, and they match to the minor unit. scenarios.reported:
Priced as of 15 September 2026 -- all four lines land on the prices already in force (SOCKET-DBL is still at €74.00; it doesn't step up to €79.00 until 1 October).

**invoice_create payload** (unit_price in MAJOR units):
```json
{
  "client": "Marina Bakery",
  "currency": "EUR",
  "items": [
    { "description": "Double socket, supplied and fitted", "quantity": 6, "unit_price": 74, "tax_rate": 23 },
    { "description": "Consumer unit replacement", "quantity": 1, "unit_price": 620, "tax_rate": 23 },
    { "description": "EICR inspection report", "quantity": 1, "unit_price": 180, "tax_rate": 23 },
    { "description": "electrician (55.00 EUR/h)", "quantity": 7.5, "unit_price": 55, "tax_rate": 23 }
  ]
}
```

**quote_create payload** (unit_price_minor in MINOR units, cents):
```json
{
  "client": "Marina Bakery",
  "currency": "EUR",
  "items": [
    { "description": "Double socket, supplied and fitted", "quantity": 6, "unit_price_minor": 7400, "tax_rate": 23, "currency": "EUR" },
    { "description": "Consumer unit replacement", "quantity": 1, "unit_price_minor": 62000, "tax_rate": 23, "currency": "EUR" },
    { "description": "EICR inspection report", "quantity": 1, "unit_price_minor": 18000, "tax_rate": 23, "currency": "EUR" },
    { "description": "electrician (55.00 EUR/h)", "quantity": 7.5, "unit_price_minor": 5500, "tax_rate": 23, "currency": "EUR" }
  ]
}
```

**Net:** €1,656.50 **VAT (23%):** €381.00 **Total:** €2,037.50

**Watch out for:**
- **The 23% VAT is a fallback, not a rate set on any of these SKUs.** It's coming from the shared business profile default, not something I confirmed against these specific items. Worth a quick sanity check that 23% is genuinely right for all four lines (goods+fit vs. a report vs. labour can sometimes differ) before it goes out.
- **Nothing has actually been posted yet** -- this only resolved the pricing. You (or I) still need to call `invoice_create` on the invoice server or `quote_create` on the quotes server with the matching payload above.
- **Don't cross the payloads** -- invoice_create wants `unit_price` in whole euros (e.g. `74`), quote_create wants `unit_price_minor` in cents (e.g. `7400`). Swapping them under- or over-charges by 100x.
- **Date sensitivity:** this was priced for 15 September. If the job slips to October 1 or later, SOCKET-DBL becomes €79.00 and the whole total needs re-resolving.

A client that forwards the link on the strength of the name hands a customer an .html attachment, and a link that any holder can open (fetched with no Authorization header it also returns 200, by design of the one-hour capability URL) is the thing being forwarded. Every hosted document server has the same Workers limit; this round records it against catalogue because the tool NAME is the format it cannot produce, whereas work-order's completion_report_text in round 36 promised text and served text.

bottom_line: 18 of 18 hosted on a Pro key, against round 37's 14 of 18 over stdio on the free tier. The whole of round 37's gap was the undated question; this round asked it twice with the ladder's newest row booked for a date still in the future, so the newest row on file and the row in force were different numbers, and both times the client answered from the in_force block: 74.00 today, 79.00 queued for 1 October, the 2025 row historical. The dated question picked three different rows including a future one and relayed the pre-ladder date as a refusal. lines_resolve on a real 23 percent profile rate came back as two payloads reproduced field for field, unit_price 74 against unit_price_minor 7400, with the 100x gap stated in both directions and the server's net, VAT and total repeated to the cent rather than re-added. The price list download was fetched as bytes and carries the business heading and every in-force row; the client said out loud that the hosted endpoint serves an HTML print-to-PDF page rather than a PDF, which is the round's one server-side finding, proposed as D-R97 (low), with a second low proposal D-R98 for the document printing the issuer twice and omitting the booked later row. The one measurement caveat is that the standalone undated prompt made no tool call and read the previous turn's same-day in_force block, which is right today and would be wrong after 1 October in a resumed conversation.
